preamble: Assibilation of a fronted (palatalized) voiced velar to the alveolar affricate [dz]. The textbook case is the Slavic second and third velar palatalizations, in which *g before front vowels (or after them, in the third palatalization) was fronted and then became *dz; the affricate survives in the oldest Old Church Slavonic texts and in Lechitic (Polish pieniądz, ksiądz), elsewhere simplifying to z.

examples.note: Germanic loanwords in -ing- underwent the third palatalization; Polish keeps the affricate, Czech peníz has z.
Same development; Czech kněz shows the later simplification dz > z.
